name: Sure As Ship for WooCommerce
author: sureasship

sections.description:
Sure As Ship for WooCommerce connects your store to Sure As Ship, a Canadian shipping platform. Your customers see live commercial rates from Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator at checkout, and you book labels without leaving WooCommerce.

Features

  • Live rates at checkout from the carriers you choose, in both the classic and block checkout
  • Pass your discounted rate on to customers, or show retail and keep the difference
  • Markup percentage and flat handling fee
  • Book the service the customer picked with one click, or automatically in the background when an order reaches Processing or Completed
  • Book orders placed with any other shipping method from the order screen
  • Download labels; Canada Post QR codes for printing at a post office
  • Return labels and Canada Post return QR codes
  • Tracking number added to the order, the customer’s order page and their emails
  • Where each parcel is (Delivered, In transit, Out for delivery…) and its carrier scans on the order screen, with a Refresh tracking button
  • Several ship-from locations, chosen per order
  • Optional packing into the boxes you use, each with its own empty weight, and a warning for any product that fits none of them
  • Customs information for cross-border shipments, with per-product HS codes
  • Signature, Saturday delivery and hold-for-pickup options, and scheduled carrier pickups

What you need

  • A Sure As Ship account and an API key from it
  • A ship-from address in Canada, or in the US for US-registered accounts
  • Shipments are billed by Sure As Ship to your account. The plugin itself is free. A test API key books sandbox labels that are never charged, so you can try everything first.

External services

This plugin needs the Sure As Ship API (https://sureasship.com/api/ecommerce/v1), operated by Sure As Ship, to work. Nothing is sent until you save an API key, and nothing is sent that is not needed for the action below.

  • At checkout and on the cart page, to show rates: the ship-from postal code, province and country; the destination street address (once the shopper has entered it), postal code, city, province, country and company name; the weight, dimensions and WooCommerce product ID of each item in the cart; and your rate settings (carriers, packing method and boxes, delivery options). For a destination outside the ship-from country, each cart item’s name, price, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link is also sent, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them, so prepaid US and EU duties can be estimated. The street lets carriers such as UPS tell a business address from a home and price it the way they will bill it. No customer name, email or phone number is sent to get rates.
  • When a shipment is booked (by you, or automatically if you turn that on): the ship-from address, phone and store admin email; the customer’s name, company, shipping address, phone and email, which the carrier needs for the label; item weights, dimensions and WooCommerce product IDs; your order ID as a reference; and, for cross-border shipments, each item’s name, value, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them.
  • When products are checked against your boxes (when you choose “Check products against my boxes”, after you save a change to your boxes or packing settings, and when you save a product while “Pack into my boxes” is chosen): each product’s WooCommerce ID, weight and dimensions, and your ticked boxes, so Sure As Ship can say which products fit none of them.
  • When you choose “Send all products to Sure As Ship”: each product’s WooCommerce ID, name, SKU and customs answers (HS code, country of manufacture, CUSMA, steel and aluminum, the U.S. agency categories, part number, barcode and product page link).
  • When you test the connection, save settings, or open an order: your API key, to read your account’s name, billing status and allowed ship-from countries, and the order’s labels, customs documents, and each shipment’s status and carrier scans.
  • When you create a return, void a shipment, download a label or click Refresh tracking: the Sure As Ship shipment or return ID. Refresh tracking asks Sure As Ship to check with the carrier now.

Sure As Ship passes shipment details to the carrier you choose (Canada Post, FedEx, UPS or Purolator) so it can carry the parcel.

  • Sure As Ship terms of service: https://sureasship.com/terms
  • Sure As Ship privacy policy: https://sureasship.com/privacy

Tracking links in the order screen and customer emails point to the carrier’s own tracking page (canadapost-postescanada.ca, fedex.com, ups.com or purolator.com); they are only visited when someone clicks them.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “Sure As Ship”, then install and activate it. WooCommerce must be active.
  2. Sign in at sureasship.com and create an API key under API Keys. Use a test key first if you like.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Sure As Ship. Paste the key, click Test Connection, check your ship-from location, choose carriers, and save.
  4. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Shipping zones, edit a zone (for example “Canada”), click “Add shipping method” and choose “Sure As Ship”.

Customers in that zone now see live rates at checkout.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Sure As Ship account?

Yes. Rates and labels come from your Sure As Ship account, and shipments are billed to it. Sign up at sureasship.com.

Which carriers are supported?

Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator. Tick the ones to quote under Enabled Carriers.

Can I offer only some services, or different carriers in each shipping zone?

Yes. Under “Carriers and Services: Defaults for Every Zone”, tick “Hide Services With No Tracking” to never offer a service that has no tracking number (Canada Post’s Small Packet services), and untick any other service under Services to Offer. Each shipping zone’s Sure As Ship settings can also use its own carriers and hide more services there, for example Canada Post only to the US and Europe, and more carriers in Canada. The settings page lists the zones that have their own choices, and each zone says what it takes from the settings page. Hidden services are left out before the options shoppers see are chosen. A service your other choices already rule out is greyed out in the list, with the reason: its carrier isn’t ticked, it has no tracking and those are hidden, or, in a zone, it doesn’t go to the zone’s regions (a Canada zone greys out the US and international services). Your own tick for it is kept and comes back if you change that choice.

How do I choose which options shoppers see?

Under “Which options should shoppers see?”, choose the cheapest options from any carrier, a range of carriers (each carrier’s cheapest option first, then the next cheapest), one per carrier, or the cheapest and the fastest (the option that arrives soonest), and set “Maximum Options to Show” (0 means no limit). Or choose for each carrier: under “Options per Carrier”, set how many of each carrier’s cheapest options and of its fastest to show, for example Canada Post’s cheapest and fastest plus the cheapest from UPS; shoppers then see up to what those add up to, and the maximum is not used. “Hide Slower Options” leaves out an option when a faster one from the same carrier costs the same or less, such as Regular Parcel beside Expedited Parcel at the same price. The example under them shows what shoppers would see from made-up prices as you change them. Each shipping zone can make its own choice, or use the settings page’s. Shoppers always see the options cheapest first.

Can delivery estimates allow time to pack an order?

Yes. Set “Handling Time (business days)” to the business days you need to pack an order and get it to the carrier, from 0 to 10. Every delivery estimate shoppers see at checkout counts them, skipping weekends and holidays. With Carrier Pickup on, the pickup is booked for the day the order is ready, counted from when it was placed (this replaces the old “Pickup Delay” setting: a store with pickups on keeps its delay as its handling time). Prices don’t change. The Book Shipment dialog still shows estimates from the day you book.

Can I change the tracking email?

Yes. When a shipment is booked, the customer gets the “Order shipped (Sure As Ship)” email. Under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails you can switch it off or change its subject, heading and message, with placeholders such as {carrier} and {tracking_number}. To change its layout, copy templates/emails/sureasship-order-shipped.php from the plugin to woocommerce/emails/ in your theme. The tracking number is also added to the Completed order email unless you untick “Tracking in Order Emails”.

Does it work with the block checkout?

Yes. Rates appear in both the Cart and Checkout blocks and the classic checkout.

Can I test without being charged?

Yes. Create a test API key (it starts with sas_test_). Rates are real, but bookings use carrier sandboxes and are never charged.

What happens if Sure As Ship can’t be reached?

If you enable the fallback, customers see the flat rate you set. The same applies if Sure As Ship cannot quote for your account (it is suspended, or it is BYOC-only with no carrier account set up), and an admin notice tells you why. You then book those orders from the order screen with “Book with Sure As Ship”. If a destination or cart cannot be shipped at all, no Sure As Ship rate is shown.

What if a product has no dimensions or weight?

The default dimensions (12x8x6 in) and weight (0.5 lb) in the settings are used. Add real dimensions to your products for accurate rates.

Can I ship orders that used flat rate or free shipping?

Yes. Open the order and click “Book with Sure As Ship” to see live rates and pick a service.

Is shipping taxed?

Each Sure As Ship shipping method in a zone has its own Tax Status setting, like any WooCommerce shipping method. Prepaid duties are never taxed as shipping: they are their own line beside it, such as “US duties & taxes”.

Do I need to print a commercial invoice?

For a FedEx or UPS shipment that crosses the border, the order’s Customs Documents box says what to do, in Sure As Ship’s own words. With Automatic Customs Attestation on, FedEx receives the commercial invoice electronically. With it off, attach a paper invoice to the package; when the shipment claims CUSMA, print the one FedEx generated, listed in the same box, since it carries your CUSMA statement.

Does it work with WooPayments Multi-Currency?

Yes. A shopper who picks another currency sees Sure As Ship rates converted from your store’s currency, like your other shipping rates, and customs values are declared in your store’s currency.

How do I get my products ready for customs?

Answer the customs questions on each product’s Shipping tab, then choose “Send all products to Sure As Ship” under WooCommerce > Settings > Shipping > Sure As Ship (International Shipping). Every product goes to your Sure As Ship product catalog at once, and the page lists each product that still needs an answer, with a link to it. Fix those, then choose “Send these again”.

I installed an earlier version from sureasship.com. How do I switch?

Install this plugin and activate it. It switches the old copy off automatically, and your settings, orders and shipments carry over. Then delete the old copy (it is listed as “Sure As Ship for WooCommerce” with version 1.x).
sections.changelog:
2.0.28

  • New: “Send all products to Sure As Ship” also sends each product’s weight, size and own boxes, with your packing method and ticked boxes, so a shipment booked on the Sure As Ship website is packed as your checkout packs it. Only each product’s own measurements are sent, never the Default Weight or Default Dimensions. A weight or size you take off a product is taken off on Sure As Ship at the next send
  • New: After a send, the settings page lists the products that need a weight or size, apart from the customs answers, and says which of your boxes Sure As Ship could not take
  • New: Each booking tells Sure As Ship which products went in each package
  • Fix: The settings page and the Book dialog work with jQuery 4, which WordPress plans for version 7.3
  • Fix: The debug log no longer shows a “translation loading was triggered too early” notice after an update
  • Tested up to WordPress 7.2 and WooCommerce 11.3

2.0.27

  • Changed: Automatic booking no longer books an order with a product that has no weight or no size. It used to book it at your Default Weight or Default Dimensions, buying a label for a guessed parcel that the carrier then measures and bills. An order note and a notice now say which product, so you can add its weight and size on its Shipping tab and book the order with Book with Sure As Ship. Booking by hand still books it at the defaults
  • New: The Book dialog lists the parcels as they would be booked, under “Ships as”: the box, its size and its weight with the box’s Empty Weight. It also says which products have no weight or no size, and the default they are booked at
  • New: The check under Box Sizes also lists every product with no weight or no size, whatever the packing method. It runs by itself on your first visit to the settings after this update. While automatic booking is on and any product is listed, the Products, Orders, Settings and Plugins screens say so
  • New: “Ships in its own boxes”, on a product’s Shipping tab and on each variation, for a product that always ships in its own box or boxes, such as one boxed by its maker. Enter each box as it ships, up to 10: its size, and its weight with the product inside. Each one sold then ships as exactly those boxes, never packed into your boxes or with other items, under every packing choice. A variation with none of its own uses the product’s. Such a product is booked automatically even with no weight or size of its own, the Book dialog names each box (““Sauna”, box 1 of 2”), and customs declares the boxes’ weight when the product has none
  • Fix: The check’s summary counts in the right plural (“50 products checked: 1 fits none of your ticked boxes”)

2.0.26

  • New: Each box under Box Sizes has an Empty Weight, for the box with its tape and packing material. It is added to the weight of every parcel packed in that box, and your product weights stay as they are for customs. Max Weight is now the most the packed box may weigh, the box included, and a blank Max Weight means no limit. An Empty Weight that is not less than the Max Weight is refused
  • New: “Check products against my boxes”, under Box Sizes, lists every product that fits none of your ticked boxes and why: bigger than every box, or too heavy for the ones it fits. It runs by itself after you save a change to your boxes or packing settings, and when you save a product. While any product is listed, the Products, Orders, Settings and Plugins screens say so
  • New: The Book dialog, the booking, an order note and the order’s Sure As Ship box say when a product fits none of your ticked boxes, with the size and weight it ships at, so you hear it from the booking and not the carrier’s bill
  • Changed: The packing choices say what each one does: “No box: one parcel, items stacked” (was “Pack all items in one box”), “No box: each item is its own parcel” (was “Pack items individually”) and “Pack into my boxes” (was “Smart box packing”)
  • Fix: A ticked box with a blank Max Weight is used. Before, nothing was ever packed into it, so every item shipped at its own size
  • Fix: A product the same size as one of your boxes fits it. In a store that measures in cm or kg, a box was rounded differently from the products, so a 20 cm product did not fit a 20 cm box
  • Fix: A box you add after deleting another gets an id of its own

2.0.25

  • New: In “Services to Offer” and a zone’s “Services in This Zone”, a service your other choices already rule out is greyed out, with the reason beside it: its carrier isn’t ticked, it has no tracking and those are hidden, or, in a zone, it doesn’t go to the zone’s regions (a Canada zone greys out the US and international services). Your own tick for it is kept and comes back if you change that choice. On the settings page, a carrier that a zone ticks as its own is never greyed out, since that zone still uses the settings page’s list

2.0.24

  • New: “Choose for each carrier” under “Which options should shoppers see?”: under “Options per Carrier”, set how many of each carrier’s cheapest options and of its fastest to show, for example Canada Post’s cheapest and fastest plus the cheapest from UPS and from Purolator. Shoppers see up to what those add up to, so “Maximum Options to Show” is hidden while it is picked. Each shipping zone can set its own numbers
  • New: “Hide Slower Options” leaves out an option when a faster one from the same carrier costs the same or less, such as Regular Parcel beside Expedited Parcel at the same price. It is off until you tick it, on the settings page or in a zone
  • Fix: The radio buttons in a shipping zone’s Sure As Ship settings no longer stretch across the window
  • Fix: A zone’s example with made-up prices now changes as you change the zone’s choices, including when you go back to the settings page’s choice

2.0.23

  • New: “Handling Time (business days)”, under Rate Display Settings, adds the business days you need to pack an order and get it to the carrier to every delivery estimate shoppers see at checkout. Weekends and holidays are skipped, and prices do not change. 0, the default, adds no time
  • Changed: A carrier pickup is booked for the day the Handling Time says the order is ready, counted from when the order was placed, so an order you book later is still collected that day, or on the next pickup day once it has passed. This replaces “Pickup Delay”: a store with pickups on keeps its delay as its handling time

2.0.22

  • New: The tracking email is its own email, “Order shipped (Sure As Ship)”, under WooCommerce > Settings > Emails. Switch it off there, or change its subject, heading and message, with placeholders such as {carrier} and {tracking_number}; a theme can override its template. It replaces the customer note that carried the tracking number, whose subject never said the order had shipped, so the customer still gets one email per booking, and the order notes say whether it went
  • New: “Which options should shoppers see?” chooses the cheapest options from any carrier, a range of carriers (each carrier’s cheapest option first, then the next cheapest), one per carrier, or the cheapest and the fastest, with “Maximum Options to Show”. An example with made-up prices shows what shoppers would see as you change them. It replaces “Rate Display”, and your store keeps showing exactly what it showed before
  • New: Each shipping zone can choose its own options and maximum, for example a range of carriers in Canada and just the cheapest option to the US
  • Changed: Carriers and services are checkboxes, grouped by carrier with “Tick all” and “Untick all”, on the settings page and in each shipping zone. Choosing several no longer needs Command or Ctrl held down, and a missed click no longer drops your earlier choices
  • Changed: The settings page’s carrier and service choices are the defaults for every zone, and the page lists the zones that have their own. Each zone’s settings say what they take from the settings page, and a service hidden there shows as locked in the zone
  • Changed: “Tracking Email” is now “Tracking in Order Emails” and adds the tracking number to the Completed order email. If you had it off, the new Order shipped email starts off too

2.0.21

  • New: “Hide Services With No Tracking” never offers a service that has no tracking number (Canada Post’s Small Packet services), and “Hidden Services” leaves out any service you choose. Both are left out before “Show only cheapest rate” and the maximum number of rates, so the cheapest option shown is one you offer
  • New: Each shipping zone’s Sure As Ship settings can choose its own carriers and hide more services there, for example Canada Post only to the US and Europe, and more carriers in Canada
  • Changed: The order screen’s Book dialog and auto-book quote the carriers of the order’s shipping zone, and auto-book never books a service you hid. The Book dialog still lists every service

2.0.20

  • New: A store with its own Canada Post account also sees Sure As Ship’s Canada Post rates. Checkout shows one option per service, the cheaper of the two (your own account’s on a tie), and the order books the one the shopper chose. The Book dialog lists both and says whose account each is on
  • New: Test Connection says why your account cannot book shipments right now (for example, a paused account or a card that is needed), in Sure As Ship’s own words
  • Changed: A shipment booked with a test API key no longer sends the shopper its sandbox tracking number. The order gets a private note instead, and the order emails and My Account page leave the number out
  • Fix: A label, QR code, return label or customs document that Sure As Ship holds back (a paused account, a cancelled shipment, or a booking that was not paid for) says why, in Sure As Ship’s own words, instead of an HTTP error number

2.0.19

  • New: “If duties can’t be estimated at checkout” in the International Shipping settings. By default the rate is still shown and you pay the duty when the order is booked; choose “Hide rates that include duties.” to leave those rates out. With Hide chosen, the fallback rate is also left out for addresses where a duty would be prepaid (the U.S., and Canada Post’s EU countries)
  • New: The order screen’s Customs Documents box says what to do with the commercial invoice of a cross-border shipment, in Sure As Ship’s own words, and the booking adds the same words to the order notes. When a FedEx shipment to the U.S. without customs attestation claims CUSMA, it says to print the invoice FedEx generated and attach it, since that invoice carries your CUSMA statement, and it shows what the invoice claimed
  • Changed: The Book dialog and the booked shipment’s cost show a price as pre-tax plus tax, for example “$22.00 + $2.86 tax”, so the pre-tax part matches what the checkout quoted
  • Fix: A shipment booked with your live API key, looked at while the plugin uses a test key (or the other way round), says so in Sure As Ship’s own words in the tracking box, Refresh tracking, every download, Void and Create Return
  • Fix: A booking refused for an HS code no carrier takes says where to fix the HS code in WooCommerce, instead of suggesting a new product name
  • Fix: When Sure As Ship could not confirm with the carrier whether a label was made, the order note gives Sure As Ship’s own words and the shipment number, and auto-booking does not try again

2.0.18

  • New: Prepaid duties are their own line at checkout and on the order, beside shipping (“US duties & taxes”, or “EU duties & VAT” on Canada Post parcels to the EU). A store that charges tax on shipping no longer taxes the duties. The line follows the shipping option and the address the shopper picks, and is converted for shoppers who pick another currency with WooPayments Multi-Currency. Each option says the duty is added, for example “(+ US duties & taxes)”, and options are still listed by what the shopper pays in all. Your markup and handling fee still apply to shipping only
  • Changed: A carrier’s own customs entry charge (UPS Standard’s customs brokerage, FedEx Ground’s clearance entry fee) stays in its shipping price, as the faster UPS and FedEx services include it in theirs, so options compare like for like

2.0.17

  • New: “Send all products to Sure As Ship” in the International Shipping settings. It sends every product’s customs answers (HS code, country of manufacture, CUSMA, steel and aluminum, the U.S. agency categories, part number and barcode) to your Sure As Ship product catalog at once, so a CUSMA claim on Canada Post parcels to the U.S. can be set up before a product’s first parcel. The page then lists each product that still needs an answer, in Sure As Ship’s own words, with a link to edit it, and “Send these again” sends just those. Only each product’s own answers are sent, not the store-wide defaults
  • Fix: Shoppers who pick another currency with WooPayments Multi-Currency now see Sure As Ship rates, converted from your store’s currency like your other shipping rates. Before, they saw none, even for a local address, and the store showed a false currency-mismatch notice
  • Fix: For those orders, customs values are declared in your store’s currency, at the exchange rate WooPayments recorded on the order, so cross-border bookings are no longer refused for their currency
  • Fix: A booking Sure As Ship says is booked at the carrier but not paid or not confirmed is no longer retried by auto-booking. The order note gives Sure As Ship’s own words, which say to contact support, and the shipment number when there is one
  • Fix: A refused return label or return QR code says why in Sure As Ship’s own words, without “API error” in front
  • Fix: When Sure As Ship is briefly too busy to answer (too many requests in a minute), checkout shows your fallback rate instead of no Sure As Ship option, and auto-booking tries again a few minutes later instead of giving up

2.0.16

  • New: From November 4, 2026, Sure As Ship prepays EU duties and VAT on Canada Post parcels to Austria, Belgium, Cyprus, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovakia, Spain and Sweden. Those rates read “(includes EU duties & VAT)” at checkout, and U.S. rates still read “(includes US duties & taxes)”
  • New: “Manufacturer part or model number” on each product’s Shipping tab. EU customs asks for product identifiers from November 1, 2026, so each item’s part or model number and its GTIN, UPC, EAN or ISBN barcode are now sent with cross-border quotes and shipments, beside the SKU, which Sure As Ship uses when the part number is blank. A barcode with a wrong check digit is not sent
  • Fix: A booking refused for missing or wrong EU product identifiers says what is wrong, in Sure As Ship’s own words, and where to fix it in WooCommerce
  • Changed: The missing-HS-code notice now also covers Canada Post orders to the EU, which are quoted without prepaid duties until every product has an HS code

2.0.15

  • New: “Orders at Your Own Rates” (off by default). With auto-booking on, an order placed at one of your own shipping rates (such as Free shipping or Flat rate), or at the fallback rate, is booked with the cheapest tracked service that can take it, and an order note says which service and why. Local pickup orders are never booked. For these orders the Book dialog opens on that service
  • New: Void Shipment says how much credit went back to your Sure As Ship account, and why it is less than the charge when it is
  • Fix: Book Shipment never charges more than the price the dialog showed. If the price has gone up since, nothing is booked, you are told the new price, and the dialog shows today’s prices so you can book at the new one
  • Fix: Quotes at checkout and on the order screen include the delivery street, so UPS prices a business address as a business, the same as the booking is charged
  • Fix: U.S. rates whose duties cannot be prepaid (goods under an anti-dumping or countervailing duty order, or an import quota) are no longer offered at checkout, and a notice names the products
  • Fix: A booking or return refused for your Sure As Ship billing (such as a prepaid card on file, which Sure As Ship does not accept) or for the new-account shipment limit now says why in Sure As Ship’s own words, in the Book dialog, the order notes and the auto-booking notice
  • Changed: “Default Incoterm” now starts as “Use my Sure As Ship company setting” instead of DAP, so your company’s own setting applies. A term you already chose is kept
  • Changed: A new ship-from location starts as a residential address, so the carrier’s residential pickup charge is never under-quoted. Untick it for a business address. Saved locations keep their setting

2.0.14

  • New: When your Sure As Ship account credit (from a voided shipment or a refund) pays for some or all of a shipment, the order screen shows the credit applied and the amount paid by card under the shipment cost, and an order note says the same

2.0.13

  • New: U.S. customs details on each product’s Shipping tab, for parcels to the U.S. from October 22, 2026: the product’s steel and aluminum (percent of the product and the countries it was melted, smelted or cast in, for Section 232 duties), whether it is food, cosmetics, supplements, medicine, pet products, a children’s product, wood or plant products, or animal materials, and whether it is made in Canada and qualifies under CUSMA. Sure As Ship sends them with each U.S. quote and shipment and keeps them per product. A question you leave blank is not sent
  • New: While a product is marked as any of those regulated kinds, the product editor says US customs may ask for more information and can hold the parcel until it is given. Booking is never blocked
  • New: Warnings Sure As Ship gives with a booking, such as that one with the products it concerns, are shown when you book, stay on the order screen and are added as order notes. They clear when the shipment is voided
  • Tweak: Each customs line also carries the product’s SKU and page link
  • Fix: Changing a product’s HS code, country of manufacture or U.S. customs details now changes the U.S. duty quoted at checkout right away, instead of up to 15 minutes later

2.0.12

  • Tweak: When U.S. duties can’t be estimated at checkout because a product has no HS tariff code, an admin notice says so, links each product to fix, and points to the default HS code setting. It clears once a U.S. quote estimates the duties
  • Tweak: When Sure As Ship refuses to book a U.S. shipment for a missing HS code, the error names the items in Sure As Ship’s own words and says where to add the HS code in WooCommerce

2.0.11

  • Fix: When the carrier won’t cancel a shipment’s pickup, Void Shipment says the pickup is still scheduled (so the driver may still come) and notes it on the order, instead of reporting success
  • Tweak: Test Connection warns when your store currency differs from your Sure As Ship billing currency (checkout would otherwise show no Sure As Ship rates), and the warning and admin notice say how to fix it: set the store currency, or switch the billing currency in Company settings before your first shipment
  • Tweak: When Sure As Ship suspends your account, the admin notice gives the reason in Sure As Ship’s own words (for overdue invoices, paying in full restores the account)

2.0.10

  • New: The order screen shows where each parcel is (Delivered, In transit, Out for delivery and so on) as Sure As Ship reports it, instead of always saying Booked
  • New: Carrier scans (what happened, where and when) are listed under each shipment, and a Refresh tracking button checks with the carrier now
  • Tweak: A service without tracking (Canada Post Small Packet) says so and offers no refresh
  • Fix: When the carrier hasn’t confirmed a void, Void Shipment says so (the label may still be live, so don’t use it) and notes it on the order, instead of reporting success

2.0.9

  • New: The carrier pickup window the carrier agreed to (fitted to its own collection hours) is shown on the order and noted when the shipment is booked
  • Tweak: Pickup notes and settings name the carrier: each carrier makes its own pickup visit and charges its own fee, once per pickup date from each address
  • Fix: When Sure As Ship cannot quote for your account (suspended, or BYOC-only with no carrier account set up), checkout shows your fallback rate instead of no rate at all, and an admin notice says why

2.0.8

  • New: When a booking costs more than the checkout quote because of a carrier pickup fee, the order note names the fee
  • Tweak: Carrier Pickup settings say Canada Post pickups are supported, that pickup fees are billed to you once per stop per day (never to customers), and which pickups are free
  • Tweak: Pickup time settings explain that each carrier fits your window to its own collection hours (Canada Post collects 12:00 to 16:00)

2.0.7

  • Fix: Cross-border checkout quotes are refreshed when the cart’s value or the store currency changes, so the prepaid duty is never quoted on an old cart value

2.0.6

  • New: Export declaration number field on the order screen for Canadian exports outside the US (CBSA CERS proof of report), sent with the booking

short_description: Live Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator rates at checkout, with labels, tracking and returns from the order screen.
description:
Sure As Ship for WooCommerce connects your store to Sure As Ship, a Canadian shipping platform. Your customers see live commercial rates from Canada Post, FedEx, UPS and Purolator at checkout, and you book labels without leaving WooCommerce.

Features

  • Live rates at checkout from the carriers you choose, in both the classic and block checkout
  • Pass your discounted rate on to customers, or show retail and keep the difference
  • Markup percentage and flat handling fee
  • Book the service the customer picked with one click, or automatically in the background when an order reaches Processing or Completed
  • Book orders placed with any other shipping method from the order screen
  • Download labels; Canada Post QR codes for printing at a post office
  • Return labels and Canada Post return QR codes
  • Tracking number added to the order, the customer’s order page and their emails
  • Where each parcel is (Delivered, In transit, Out for delivery…) and its carrier scans on the order screen, with a Refresh tracking button
  • Several ship-from locations, chosen per order
  • Optional packing into the boxes you use, each with its own empty weight, and a warning for any product that fits none of them
  • Customs information for cross-border shipments, with per-product HS codes
  • Signature, Saturday delivery and hold-for-pickup options, and scheduled carrier pickups

What you need

  • A Sure As Ship account and an API key from it
  • A ship-from address in Canada, or in the US for US-registered accounts
  • Shipments are billed by Sure As Ship to your account. The plugin itself is free. A test API key books sandbox labels that are never charged, so you can try everything first.

External services

This plugin needs the Sure As Ship API (https://sureasship.com/api/ecommerce/v1), operated by Sure As Ship, to work. Nothing is sent until you save an API key, and nothing is sent that is not needed for the action below.

  • At checkout and on the cart page, to show rates: the ship-from postal code, province and country; the destination street address (once the shopper has entered it), postal code, city, province, country and company name; the weight, dimensions and WooCommerce product ID of each item in the cart; and your rate settings (carriers, packing method and boxes, delivery options). For a destination outside the ship-from country, each cart item’s name, price, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link is also sent, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them, so prepaid US and EU duties can be estimated. The street lets carriers such as UPS tell a business address from a home and price it the way they will bill it. No customer name, email or phone number is sent to get rates.
  • When a shipment is booked (by you, or automatically if you turn that on): the ship-from address, phone and store admin email; the customer’s name, company, shipping address, phone and email, which the carrier needs for the label; item weights, dimensions and WooCommerce product IDs; your order ID as a reference; and, for cross-border shipments, each item’s name, value, quantity, weight, HS code, country of manufacture, SKU and product page link, with its manufacturer part number, barcode and U.S. customs answers when you have entered them.
  • When products are checked against your boxes (when you choose “Check products against my boxes”, after you save a change to your boxes or packing settings, and when you save a product while “Pack into my boxes” is chosen): each product’s WooCommerce ID, weight and dimensions, and your ticked boxes, so Sure As Ship can say which products fit none of them.
  • When you choose “Send all products to Sure As Ship”: each product’s WooCommerce ID, name, SKU and customs answers (HS code, country of manufacture, CUSMA, steel and aluminum, the U.S. agency categories, part number, barcode and product page link).
  • When you test the connection, save settings, or open an order: your API key, to read your account’s name, billing status and allowed ship-from countries, and the order’s labels, customs documents, and each shipment’s status and carrier scans.
  • When you create a return, void a shipment, download a label or click Refresh tracking: the Sure As Ship shipment or return ID. Refresh tracking asks Sure As Ship to check with the carrier now.

Sure As Ship passes shipment details to the carrier you choose (Canada Post, FedEx, UPS or Purolator) so it can carry the parcel.

  • Sure As Ship terms of service: https://sureasship.com/terms
  • Sure As Ship privacy policy: https://sureasship.com/privacy

Tracking links in the order screen and customer emails point to the carrier’s own tracking page (canadapost-postescanada.ca, fedex.com, ups.com or purolator.com); they are only visited when someone clicks them.

upgrade_notice.2.0.28: "Send all products to Sure As Ship" also sends each product's weight, size and own boxes, with your packing method and ticked boxes, and the settings list the products that need a weight or size. Tested up to WordPress 7.2.

upgrade_notice.2.0.26: Boxes have an empty weight, the packing choices say what they do, and you are warned when a product fits none of your ticked boxes.
upgrade_notice.2.0.25: Services your other choices rule out, such as another carrier's or another country's, are greyed out in the service lists, with the reason.
upgrade_notice.2.0.24: Choose how many of each carrier's cheapest and fastest options shoppers see, hide a slower option that costs the same as a faster one, and the zone settings' radio buttons are fixed.
upgrade_notice.2.0.23: Add a handling time to every checkout delivery estimate. It also sets the carrier pickup day and replaces Pickup Delay; with pickups on, your delay carries over.
upgrade_notice.2.0.22: The tracking email becomes its own "Order shipped" email you can edit, carriers and services are checkboxes, and you choose which options shoppers see (the cheapest, a range of carriers, one per carrier, or the cheapest and the fastest), store-wide or per zone.
upgrade_notice.2.0.21: Hide services with no tracking or any service you choose, and choose carriers and hidden services for each shipping zone.
upgrade_notice.2.0.20: Stores with their own Canada Post account also see Sure As Ship's Canada Post rates. Test Connection says why booking is refused, test-key bookings no longer email a sandbox tracking number, and held-back labels say why.
upgrade_notice.2.0.19: Says what to do with the commercial invoice of cross-border shipments, including FedEx's CUSMA invoice, shows prices as pre-tax plus tax, and adds a setting for rates whose duties can't be estimated.
upgrade_notice.2.0.18: Prepaid duties are now their own line at checkout, beside shipping, and are no longer taxed as shipping.
upgrade_notice.2.0.17: Sends all your products' customs answers to Sure As Ship at once and lists what each still needs, and shows rates to shoppers who pick another currency with WooPayments Multi-Currency.
upgrade_notice.2.0.16: Ready for EU shipments: prepaid EU duties and VAT on Canada Post parcels from November 4, 2026, and the part number and barcode EU customs asks for.

upgrade_notice.2.0.14: Shows on the order screen when your Sure As Ship account credit paid for a shipment, and how much went on your card.
